text:
I ended up at this establishment not because of its specialty, but because it was nearby and the clinic was open 24/7.
After calling ahead, I was told I needed to come in since I'd been drinking alcohol. They'd give me a miracle IV and everything would be fine, like Doctor Aibolit. Upon arriving, I was met by the receptionist, whom I helped raise the blinds at the entrance. After listening to my complaints about my persistent vomiting, she immediately recommended an IV for 18,500 baht. I said I couldn't afford that and would go to the hospital. The receptionist called someone named Taras Sergeyevich, and the price dropped to 5,000 baht. I was so exhausted I had to agree. A man arrived, introduced himself as a doctor at the clinic, and quickly processed my transfer to Sberbank at a rate of 2.9. They sat me down in a chair just like in the ad, and their ad is beautiful, just like Guf in a cap. They started the drip, and I went to the bathroom a couple of times with the IV to puke, then asked for a bucket. The person who accepted my transfer brought me a large office bucket with a bag and garbage inside, into which I proceeded to puke. The man, who introduced himself as a doctor, said, "Yeeesss, serious poisoning," and left the hospital. I continued lying on the chair, just like in the ad, except I couldn't smile, only gagging. The girl replied, "Well, we'll treat you for what you paid." Knowing it wouldn't do any good, I asked to disconnect the system and let me go to the hospital, since I had received confirmation from the insurance company. The girl stubbornly continued to hold me back, insisting that I'd feel better any minute, that I'd already paid, and that I should receive the full amount. Well, what can I do? I couldn't force myself to escape. I lay on the chair and vomited into the office bucket until the saline solution ran out. Just for fun, I lifted the bucket; it was about three liters. Wasn't it hard to carry?
I'm familiar with drug addiction and detoxing patients.
Regarding the service you provided me, you "doctors" wasted my precious time, blurring the picture for a proper diagnosis and further treatment.
Of course, I received treatment in the hospital; it was seafood poisoning, but that's another story.

I'd recommend anyone suffering from this to regular, small Thai clinics. They'll give you IVs for 1,000-1,500 baht and add vitamins as a bonus. They won't offer Phenazepam, of course, but they have plenty of Diazepam and Haloperidol.
Stay safe, and all the best!
